3D · Survival · Exploration · Godot 4

Find the lost traces on the red planet.

Mars Explorer is a 3D exploration game built on real NASA/USGS Martian terrain. Dig, build, survive, recover lost space hardware and keep in touch with Earth. Play solo or with up to 8 friends.

The Story

Orbital cameras have been imaging Mars for years. Comparing new frames against the archive, a NASA team spots objects that belong to no active mission: a wheel, a scrap of foil, even a sample tube. The orbiters pinpoint the locations, but someone has to go there and retrieve each item.

The game opens with a cinematic introduction of about a minute: a Houston briefing, orbital imagery, suiting up, the rocket launch and the landing on Mars. You can skip it if you like.

Crew: Dr. Amara Okonkwo (Mission Director), Cmdr. Daniel Reyes, Dr. Leyla Hasanova (geologist) and Kenji Mori (flight engineer).

Signal delay is 13 minutes — Houston's replies arrive in the game with a realistic lag.

Core loop

Explore→Dig→Collect→Craft→Build→Survive→Find artifacts

Your goal is to locate and document every lost artifact. Each discovery grants a short quiz and XP, and the final screen determines your rank.

Key Features

Every system is interconnected: oxygen depends on your base, food depends on the greenhouse, and the greenhouse depends on the minerals you dig up.

⛏️

Terrain Digging and Building

Reshape the ground with the digging tool (left click) and build up terrain with the blue beam (right click). Brush radius is 1–2.5 m and grows with your level. Changes appear identically for everyone in multiplayer.

💎

7 Types of Minerals

Iron, copper, silicon, water ice, titanium, gold and uranium are hidden 1.6–3.5 m below the surface. Each deposit holds 2–7 pieces, and the pieces fly to you one by one.

🫁

Oxygen and Tether

While tethered to the ship, your oxygen is unlimited. If you wander more than 80 m away, the tether snaps and you have 30 seconds of air. It reconnects automatically when you return.

🌱

Greenhouse and Food

Your hunger bar fills in 5 minutes. Food comes only from the greenhouse. Upgrade it up to level 4: bed count increases and growth time drops from 2:30 to 1:00.

🛰️

Real NASA Data

Soil reports are based on real measurements from Pathfinder, Phoenix and Curiosity. For terrain, you can load a HiRISE DEM file.

🗺️

Minimap and Task Bar

A circular minimap shows the ship, greenhouse, base and other players. The task bar lists undiscovered artifacts, with the nearest one first.

🌅

A Real Martian Day

A game day lasts 24 hours 39 minutes, tracked by the Sol counter on the left. Solar panels go dark at night, and you have to wait for evening to sleep.

🎨

High-End Graphics

Procedural Martian sky, Phobos and Deimos, volumetric dust haze, SSAO, 4-cascade shadows and soft shadow edges. Everything can be turned off for low-end PCs.

💾

Automatic Saving

The game saves every 30 seconds and on exit: position, inventory, structures, greenhouse, dug terrain and XP. You always continue where you left off.

Build a Modular Base

Craft parts at the Fabricator, then connect them end to end. You can walk inside the modules, doors open and close, and a nearby Solar or RTG unit supplies power.

Hab Module

A bed. Sleep from sunset until morning.

Lab Module

Analyzes resources (3 s), +12 XP.

Storage Tank

Adds +900 capacity to the base's oxygen reserve.

Hub and Connector

A four-door junction and a 3 m connecting tunnel.

Habitat Dome

A dome that extends the cable network and oxygen supply.

Solar · RTG · MOXIE

Solar works only by day, RTG runs around the clock. MOXIE produces oxygen.

Progression and Perks

XP comes from quizzes, soil reports, lab analysis and sending data to Earth. Each level increases your speed by 0.4 and unlocks an additional perk.

Level 2 — digging radius +30%
Level 3 — see nearby minerals on the minimap
Level 4 — crafting is 20% cheaper
Level 5 — keep 50% of your resources after death
Level 6 — 60 seconds of reserve oxygen in your pack
Level 7 — plants grow 20% faster
Level 8 — tether extends from 80 m to 96 m
Level 9 — speed +20%
Level 10 — hunger rises 10% slower

Finale: The Rank System

When every artifact has been found, an animated summary screen appears, tallying XP, level, quiz accuracy, resources extracted, distance traveled and dangerous moments. Based on the result, you earn 1–3 stars and a rank.

Support CrewRookieExplorer (40%+)Mission Commander (80%+)Mars Legend (100%)

The Planet's Own Events

🌪️

Dust Storm

Based on NASA/JPL facts. After a warning, the sky darkens, visibility drops to about 45 m and dust accumulates on your helmet visor. Solar panels go offline while the RTG keeps running. Storms begin from the second sol.

🤖

Rover and Soil Report

A Spirit/Opportunity-type rover analyzes the soil every 5 sols. Collect the report and send it to Earth from the ship. Every report is based on real NASA data.

📡

Deep Space Comm Dish

After sol 8 it appears 28–40 m from the ship. Send mission data once per sol to earn +25 XP.

A Shared World with Friends

When one player does something, it changes for everyone. Oxygen, hunger and XP remain personal.

Shared Terrain

Digging and building are synchronized for everyone. When a new player joins, the host sends them the current terrain.

Shared Resources

A mineral or lost artifact that is picked up disappears for everyone. To pass resources to a teammate, use “Give to” in your inventory.

Shared Base

Modules, the greenhouse and doors are the same for everyone. The time of day follows the host's clock.

8 Players

One host and 7 joiners. Helmet lights are visible to others, and teammates appear as yellow dots on the minimap.

To play from separate homes, the host forwards UDP port 24565 on their router and runs open_firewall.bat as administrator. The game copies your public IP automatically.

Controls
